body:
Redline round 4

Reviewed the whole pull request. Rounds 1 to 3 are already on this PR; this run starts at round 4.

The coverage pass over the whole pull request at 4227e11 returned 11 candidates: 11 verified, 0 could not be confirmed, 0 refuted, 0 collapsed into items already reported or settled, 0 already tracked.

Round 3's fixes are in place: seven of its eight findings are closed at the lines cited, and R3-5 still holds and is carried. All 11 coverage candidates were verified, and most sit where #93's new decisions meet older code. NOT_YOURS now reaches the plan approver and the resolve agent, whose jobs reopen a shaper's decision. An unresolved override, a stale deferred entry and a renamed id fall through bookkeeping written before declines existed. The human-review path still reads newHead where the main loop now reads what was fixed. The Docs and Version steps hold (0.3.0 against main's 0.2.4, a Docs entry for every touched plugin file), and the repository has no scheduled or queued work.

### Correctness (7)

- **R4-4** · correctness · medium · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:1748` · The resolve prompt says to apply an overruled decline, then that a shaper's decline is never reopened
- **R4-5** · correctness · medium · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:1775` · The plan approver is told the shaper's fix, decline and deferral are never reopened, though its bounces reopen them
- **R4-6** · correctness · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:2310` · A renamed reviewer id can collide with an id another finding already has
- **R4-8** · correctness · medium · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:2945` · A disposition override the resolve agent cannot apply stops the run with no question to answer
- **R4-9** · correctness · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3111` · A deferred entry beside a decline is listed under Deferred as shipped
- **R4-11** · correctness · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3275` · The handoff's overrule line names the runner's login, so a teammate's reply is not read
- **R4-12** · correctness · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3726` · A human review pass that fixed nothing still runs and posts a final nit pass over an empty diff

### Other items (4)

- **R4-1** · nit · low · confirmed · `skills/redline-revise/SKILL.md:19` · The human-review finding template still writes needsDecision, which #93 removed from the finding contract
- **R4-2** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:446` · rulesBlock still says a rule-covered finding is never fixed or deferred, and leaves decline out
- **R4-3** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:1135` · With no login, decisionSentence's fallback starts a sentence in lowercase
- **R4-10** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3165` · A correctness fix the person changes to accept on the plan dial still buys a round

### Carried forward from earlier rounds (0 correctness, 1 nit)

- **R4-7** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:2878` · checkWhy runs after the spec-status agent call, so a refused reason first costs that call · first reported as R3-5

### Resolved from earlier rounds

- **R3-1** An older install's prior-findings cannot read the 0.3.0 finding line, and nothing says so: docs/upgrading.md now has the section 'Two Redline versions on one pull request (0.3.0)' (lines 27-29), which says an older prior-findings cannot read the 0.3.0 line and to continue such a pull request with 0.3.0 or later.
- **R3-2** wouldConfirm is posted raw in the inline comment, so a bare @-word in it notifies an account: commentBody now passes wouldConfirm through postedText (workflows/redline-loop.js:1119), as findingLine does.
- **R3-3** With coverage off the prompt forbids the decline reopen that the agent file and README state without condition: agents/redline-reviewer.md:22, README.md:103 and docs/running.md:45 now say the decline reopen needs a coverage candidate and that with coverage off a declined finding stays settled, as the prompt does.
- **R3-4** A left-out candidate with no summary or scenario is minted as a correctness finding with an empty title and description: accountCoverage's mint now falls back to 'coverage candidate <index> (no summary given)' for the title and to MINTED_NO_CLAIM for the description (workflows/redline-loop.js:1528, 1590).
- **R3-6** The handoff's overrule line always names the /redline-revise alias, which a repository may not have: The overrule line now names the namespaced `/redline:redline-revise` (workflows/redline-loop.js:3275).
- **R3-7** A decline overruled at a reshape's decisions stop changes prompts before that stop, so the relaunch does not replay to it: handoffResult lists no declines at a stop after the round's plan approver ran (`declined: outcome.afterApproval ? [] : roundDeclines`, line 3679; afterApproval is set at lines 2945 and 3002) and names them in declinedAfterRun.
- **R3-8** result().rounds[].findings carries scope-declined items, which the skill's summaries count or leave out unmarked: result() returns each round's scope-declined items under `scoped` (workflows/redline-loop.js:2216), and the skill's review-only and done summaries name them (skills/redline/SKILL.md:170, 240).

Each item has an inline comment with the detail or, where GitHub could not anchor it, sits under Not placed inline below. Redline replies in the item's thread, or in a PR comment that opens with its marker, with what it decided and why.

**R4-1** · nit · low · confirmed

**The human-review finding template still writes needsDecision, which #93 removed from the finding contract**

The finding template this skill builds for each teammate comment still carries `"needsDecision": false` (line 19). This pull request removed the field from FINDING_SCHEMA, the reviewer, the shaper and `skills/redline/SKILL.md`. R1-4 fixed it in that file only (6a8c63a); this file is not in that fix or in this pull request's diff. Human findings never pass through review(), so the `delete f.needsDecision` at workflows/redline-loop.js:2321 never runs on them. The field reaches humanShapePrompt's findings JSON (workflows/redline-loop.js:1682), and no instruction defines it. The loop test's human fixtures carry it too (tests/loop-test.mjs:904, 1149, 2096, 2249, 2372). It is always false, so nothing behaves differently today. Two readings: it is a leftover to remove, or it stays on purpose. The pull request says a human review pass's own prompts are as they were, and removing the field changes the bytes of that pass's shaper prompt.

Proposed fix: Drop `"needsDecision": false` from the template at line 19 and from the loop test's human fixtures. Or record in the #93 spec's shape.md that the human pass keeps it so its prompts stay unchanged.

The cause is in code this pull request did not change.

**R4-2** · nit · low · confirmed

**rulesBlock still says a rule-covered finding is never fixed or deferred, and leaves decline out**

The ask-rules text goes into the shaper's, the reshape's and the plan approver's prompts (rulesBlock, line 446). It says a covered finding is 'never fixed or deferred by Redline', and that the approver bounces 'a task that writes under a paths rule or fixes a finding a prose rule covers'. This pull request made decline a disposition and updated the same rule elsewhere: the shaper's rule 7 says 'never fix, decline or defer' (agents/redline-shaper.md:29), the skill says 'never fixed, declined or deferred by Redline' (skills/redline/SKILL.md:98), and forceAskRules's comment names decline (line 2698). Line 446 is unchanged by the diff.

The prompt's positive sentence ('in the shaper's JSON it is ask') still directs an ask, so the omission alone does not license a decline. Little stands behind that sentence for a prose rule. forceAskRules forces a prose rule only from the shaper's own askRule tag (lines 2719-2720); it does not read the reviewer's tag. A decline has no task, so neither rulesBlock's approver sentence nor the approver's point 5 ('a fix or defer task', agents/redline-plan-approver.md:20) can bounce it. Before this pull request, every non-ask disposition had a task the approver could bounce.

So a shaper that declines a prose-covered finding without tagging it is posted 'declined:' and its thread is resolved at Finish. The inline comment meanwhile says the finding is left to the person (commentBody, line 1126, reads the reviewer's tag through ruleOf). Conditions: a repository with a prose ask rule, and a shaper that declines a covered finding against its prompt and its agent file.

Proposed fix: Say 'never fixed, declined or deferred by Redline' in rulesBlock. Add that a decline of a finding a prose rule covers is a bounce, in rulesBlock's approver sentence and in point 5 of agents/redline-plan-approver.md. Optionally have forceAskRules also read the reviewer's askRule tag (ruleOf) for prose rules. The prompts change only in repositories that declare ask rules.

The cause is in code this pull request did not change.

**R4-3** · nit · low · confirmed

**With no login, decisionSentence's fallback starts a sentence in lowercase**

This pull request changed decisionSentence's fallback for a Redline round from 'The author chose: ...' to `${personLabel} chose: ...` (line 1135). With no login, personLabel is 'the person running Redline'. In a human-review run's final nit pass, which is a Redline round, it is 'the author' (line 190). The reply then reads 'Redline round 2: the person running Redline chose: Keep it. No code change. · decided by: the person running Redline' (replyBody, line 1295), and the handoff line carries the same sentence (describeOutcome, line 2567). R1-17 fixed the same lowercase start in capComment only (line 3388), so this is a second site with the same cause, not a reopening of that fix. Conditions: args.login is empty and a decision has empty notes. The skill always passes a login from `redline-gh.sh login` and always writes notes, and autopilot decisions carry notes, so only a hand-built relaunch reaches it.

Proposed fix: Capitalise the label where it starts the sentence, as capComment does since R1-17: `${human ? 'The author' : personLabel.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + personLabel.slice(1)} chose: ${decision.choice}.` Add a loop check for no login and a decision with no notes.

**R4-4** · correctness · medium · confirmed

**The resolve prompt says to apply an overruled decline, then that a shaper's decline is never reopened**

For a Redline round, resolvePrompt lists the person's disposition overrides and says 'a finding the shaper declined is overruled the same way' (line 1742). It then closes with decideRule(pass), which for a Redline round is NOT_YOURS (lines 343, 354, 1748): 'A decision already made, the shaper's own included (a fix, a decline with its reason, a deferral), is applied as recorded and never reopened.' Overruling a decline is exactly reopening the shaper's decline, so one prompt says both. Before this pull request the line carried NEVER_DECIDE, which has no 'never reopened' clause. The agent file says the overrule is applied (agents/redline-resolve.md:14, 21); the prompt's last rule says the opposite.

A resolve agent that follows the last rule does one of two things. It keeps the decline, which is posted 'declined:' and its thread resolved at Finish, against the person's line. Or it lists the finding under unresolved, which on guided gives a stop with no question on it (R4-8).

The implementer and the plan approver are shown the effective disposition (lines 2958-2961, 2970, 3053), so the overruled decline reaches them as fix and the clash is weaker there. The loop test scripts the resolve agent, so whether a real one keeps the decline is not measured; the contradiction is in the prompt text.

Proposed fix: In resolvePrompt's Redline branch, replace NOT_YOURS with the rule the resolve agent needs: a pending decision is the person's; a disposition override is the person's decision and replaces the shaper's, a decline included; every other decision is applied as recorded. Pin the sentence in the loop test beside the existing 'Disposition overrides' check (tests/loop-test.mjs:2297).

**R4-5** · correctness · medium · confirmed

**The plan approver is told the shaper's fix, decline and deferral are never reopened, though its bounces reopen them**

A Redline round's planPrompt opens its rule with NOT_YOURS (line 1775): the shaper's own fix, decline and deferral are 'applied as recorded and never reopened' (line 343). Before this pull request the prompt carried NEVER_DECIDE, which has no such clause.

The approver's agent file, changed in this pull request, lists bounces that reopen exactly those decisions (agents/redline-plan-approver.md:17):
- a disproportionate fix;
- a decline whose reason a teammate cannot check;
- a decline of a finding still unconfirmed and serious if true ('that one is the person's to decide');
- a refactor that fails one of the four tests.

The same prompt's next sentence makes a decline with no reason a teammate can read a bounce, which contradicts 'never reopened' within one paragraph. The approver is the only layer after the shaper that checks a decline against the unconfirmed-serious case. The workflow checks only that a decline has a reason (checkDispositions, lines 2592-2595).

When the approver does bounce a decline, the reshape is told 'Decisions already recorded as decided in shape.md stay as they are' (line 1708, context). The shaper records its declines under Decisions as decided by redline (agents/redline-shaper.md:23), so the reshape can keep the decline. After maxPlanAdjustments bounces the run stops at 'approve' (lines 2985-2987). The prompt text is traced; how a real approver weighs the two instructions is not measured.

Proposed fix: Give the approver's Redline branch its own sentence in place of NOT_YOURS: a pending decision is the person's and the approver never decides it; the person's decisions (the roundDecisions block) are applied as recorded; the shaper's own dispositions are what the approver checks, as its instructions say. In reshapePrompt's Redline branch, say that a decided entry an adjustment names is decided again. Pin both in the loop test.

**R4-7** · nit · low · confirmed

**checkWhy runs after the spec-status agent call, so a refused reason first costs that call**

First reported as R3-5 in Redline round 3.

At this head, revise() still runs checkSpec, which starts the `spec status` GitHub agent (line 2671), before forceAskRules and checkWhy: lines 2876-2878 after the shape, and 2994-2996 after a reshape. forceAskRules reads only record, pass, inScope and shaped, so it and checkWhy could run first. In this order, a why_human that checkWhy refuses costs one agent call before the stop. checkWhy also has to be passed the shaper's label explicitly, since lastLabel names the spec check (R2-9, line 2651). The shaper's schema already refuses a reason outside ROUND_WHY and the rule reasons (judgmentCallSchema, line 651, used by SHAPE_SCHEMAS at line 722), so the throw is reached only when that structured output is not enforced. Round 3's shape.md records a decline of this finding in its Declined section: the spec check's diagnosis of a halted shaper (#57) runs first and is worth the one call. No reply reached the thread, so the finding is carried. It is a cost and an ordering point, not wrong behaviour.

Proposed fix: Run forceAskRules and checkWhy before checkSpec at both sites, keep the explicit shaper label, and check that the loop test's replay prefixes still hold. Or post round 3's recorded decline as this finding's decision.

**R4-8** · correctness · medium · confirmed

**A disposition override the resolve agent cannot apply stops the run with no question to answer**

When the resolve agent returns an id under unresolved, resolveWith hands back `pending: newCalls.filter((call) => ids.includes(call.id))` (line 2945). An override is not a call, so an unresolved override is left out of pending. handoffResult then returns judgmentCalls [] and decisionsNeeded [] (lines 3648, 3682). It also leaves the overruled decline out of `declined`, since its decision carries a disposition (line 3664). The id appears only in `unresolved` (line 3681), which the skill never reads (nothing in skills/ or docs/ mentions it).

Trace on guided:
1. At the first stop the person types `R1-7: defer. keep it small`.
2. On relaunch, overridesFor picks it up (line 2916).
3. The first resolve finds the mitigation too unclear and leaves it pending, as agents/redline-resolve.md:29 tells it to.
4. The stop has nothing to present, so every call in decisionsNeeded counts as answered, and the skill asks for `relaunch` (skills/redline/SKILL.md:214).
5. The relaunch has the same args, so the resolve prompt is identical and replays its cached unresolved result. The run stops at the same empty hand-off every time.

The filter predates this pull request (main line 2758), and a plan-dial override could already reach it. This pull request changed the line (adding shaped and afterApproval) and adds a new way in: the typed decline overrule at a decisions stop. On autopilot the same path is a stageError that names 'the shaper's recommendation' (line 2943).

Proposed fix: Carry an unresolved override into the hand-off: list it in the stop's result, for example under `declined` with the resolve agent's why, or as an entry the skill must ask again. Have the skill present `unresolved` and ask the person to restate the line before `relaunch`. Loop check: a guided stop with a typed defer overrule that the resolve returns unresolved names that id in the hand-off.

**R4-9** · correctness · low · confirmed

**A deferred entry beside a decline is listed under Deferred as shipped**

Every entry in the round's `deferred` list goes into deferredAll, whatever its finding's final disposition (lines 3109-3112). outcomesFor files a finding as deferred only when its disposition is defer (line 2541). So a declined finding with a deferred entry is posted 'declined: <reason>', and the handoff also lists it under '### Deferred (mitigated now, full fix left open)' as 'shipped <mitigation>' (lines 3283-3285). The skill's `done` walk then offers it as a deferral whose mitigation shipped (skills/redline/SKILL.md:240).

The entry gets there two ways:
- The shaper returns a decline with a stray deferred entry. Nothing checks deferred ids against defer dispositions (checkDispositions, lines 2585-2620).
- A reshape re-sorts a defer to a decline. Line 3004 keeps every earlier deferred entry the reshape's list does not name, so the first shaper's entry survives.

The implementer's and the approver's prompts also get the stale entry beside the decline (lines 1771, 1849). Both lines predate this pull request (main lines 2816 and 2921), where a defer re-sorted to fix showed the same double listing. This pull request adds decline, a disposition with no task and no commit, so the Deferred line now claims a mitigation that never shipped.

Proposed fix: Push to deferredAll only the items outcomesFor files as deferred: move the loop after outcomesFor and filter on `outcomes[item.id].kind === 'deferred'`. At line 3004, drop an earlier entry whose finding the reshape sorted to something other than defer. A warning in checkDispositions for a deferred id whose disposition is not defer would show the stray case. Loop check: a reshape that re-sorts R1-4 from defer to decline leaves it out of Deferred.

The cause is in code this pull request did not change.

**R4-10** · nit · low · confirmed

**A correctness fix the person changes to accept on the plan dial still buys a round**

`bought` reads the shaper's own disposition before any override (shaperOwn, lines 3131 and 3165). So a correctness item the shaper sorted as fix, which the person changed to accept on the plan dial, still buys the next round: a coverage pass and a verify at an unchanged head (range.empty, line 3920), and one more round toward the cap. A decline the person overrules to fix also buys, through finalOwn, so the two overrides act differently.

Two readings. In the first, the code is as intended. It follows decision 1 of the #93 spec ('a new correctness item that the shaper fixes or puts to the person ... whatever the person answered', agent-os/specs/2026-11-13-1139-93-verify-facts-shaper-decides/shape.md:42) and docs/running.md:43 ('This holds whatever you answered ... after a round you answered with "no change"'). The comment at lines 3127-3130 says the shaper's disposition is read on purpose: the finder was still producing correctness material. In the second, a plan-dial accept takes the item off the table: nothing was fixed or put to the person as a call, and the extra round is only a cost.

No loop check covers a plan-dial accept of a fix (tests/loop-test.mjs, section 19). It is a cost, not wrong output.

Proposed fix: Keep it, and say so in docs/running.md:43 (a fix you change to accept on the plan dial still buys the round). Or exclude it: in the shaperOwn branch, skip an item whose finalOwn is accept. Either way, add a loop check for a plan-dial accept of a correctness fix.

**R4-11** · correctness · low · confirmed

**The handoff's overrule line names the runner's login, so a teammate's reply is not read**

The Declined by Redline heading tells the reader to reply in the thread, then run `/redline:redline-revise <pr> review @<login>` filled with the login of the person running Redline (line 3275). The handoff is addressed to the teammate ('`@<teammate>`, over to you', line 3220). The `@login` selector keeps only comments by that login (scripts/redline-gh.sh:428-432). A teammate who replies in a declined thread, and then runs the posted command or has the runner run it, gets a pass that does not see their reply. When the reply is the only open comment, the pass stops with 'nothing to revise for that selector' (skills/redline-revise/SKILL.md:16). docs/running.md:114 says 'A teammate overrules the same way from their own review', meaning with their own login, but the posted line never says so. The PR description states the after-run door as `review @<login>` without saying whose login.

Proposed fix: Say whose login goes in the command, e.g. 'then run `/redline:redline-revise <pr> review @<the login that replied>`' (with `review @<runner>` for a reply of the runner's own). Update the loop checks that pin the line, and docs/running.md:114.

**R4-12** · correctness · low · confirmed

**A human review pass that fixed nothing still runs and posts a final nit pass over an empty diff**

The human-review path runs its final nit pass when `outcome.newHead` is set (line 3726). newHead is the last of the round's new commits (line 3152). The implementer always commits the spec folder as task 1 (agents/redline-implementer.md:17), so newHead is set even when every comment was `none` or an ask answered with no change.

The nit pass then reviews `git diff <startSha>..<newHead> -- ':/' ':(top,exclude)agent-os/specs'` (line 1333), which is empty when the only commit is the spec folder. It posts a 'Redline round N' review for that diff (line 3745), which uses up a round number later runs would have used. The summary says 'Final nit pass (Redline round N): no correctness bugs.' (line 3373), where humanSummary's own sentence for this case is 'No commits, so no final nit pass.' (line 3371).

In this pull request the main loop moved to the commits that fixed something (`fixed`, lines 3166 and 3910; R1-20), but this site still reads newHead. The line is unchanged from main (line 3429).

Proposed fix: Gate the human path's nit pass on `outcome.fixed.length > 0`, as the main loop gates on fixedAny, and keep newHead as the range's end. Reword the no-pass sentence to 'No fix was committed, so no final nit pass.' Loop check: a human pass whose only finding is `none` posts no Redline round and gets that sentence.

The cause is in code this pull request did not change.
